desc:
Rectangular buildings stand on a flat line. Building [left, right, height] occupies the range from left to right (right edge exclusive) and has the given height. Buildings may overlap, nest or touch, and they come in no particular order.

The skyline is the outline of the union of all buildings. Describe it as a list of key points [x, h] sorted by x: x is a position at which the outline height changes, and h is the new height from x onward (up to the next key point). The last key point always has height 0. Two consecutive key points never have the same height, and there is at most one key point per x.

buildings = [[2, 9, 10], [3, 7, 15], [5, 12, 12], [15, 20, 10], [19, 24, 8]]
result    = [[2, 10], [3, 15], [7, 12], [12, 0], [15, 10], [20, 8], [24, 0]]

With no buildings the skyline is empty: return [].
constraints: buildings[i] = [left, right, height] with 0 ≤ left < right ≤ 2<sup>31</sup> - 1
hints: The outline height can only change at a left or right edge of some building. At such an x you need the tallest building that covers it.
Sweep the sorted distinct edge coordinates. Keep the buildings that have started in a max-heap keyed by height, so the current outline height is the top of the heap.

Remove finished buildings lazily: while the top of the heap has right ≤ x, pop it. Compare the resulting height (0 for an empty heap) with the previous outline height and output [x, height] only when it differs.
editorial: Between two neighbouring edge coordinates the outline is flat, so it is enough to evaluate the height at each distinct edge coordinate x, in increasing order. The height at x is the maximum height among buildings with left ≤ x < right.

Sort the buildings by left edge and keep a max-heap of (-height, right). For each x: push all buildings with left ≤ x, then pop from the top while right ≤ x. Entries that are expired but buried below the top cannot affect the maximum, and they are removed as soon as they surface, so this lazy deletion is correct. The top gives the current height (0 if the heap is empty).

Output [x, height] when the height differs from the previous one. That automatically merges adjacent buildings of equal height, keeps a single key point where one building ends and a taller or shorter one starts at the same x, and ends with a height-0 point. Sorting and heap operations make it O(n log n) time with O(n) space.
solution:
import heapq


def getSkyline(buildings):
    bs = sorted(buildings)
    xs = sorted({x for l, r, h in bs for x in (l, r)})
    heap = []
    i = 0
    result = []
    prev = 0
    for x in xs:
        while i < len(bs) and bs[i][0] <= x:
            heapq.heappush(heap, (-bs[i][2], bs[i][1]))
            i += 1
        while heap and heap[0][1] <= x:
            heapq.heappop(heap)
        cur = -heap[0][0] if heap else 0
        if cur != prev:
            result.append([x, cur])
            prev = cur
    return result
